read: docs/RESEARCH/people-1812-3467/day.json (the gathering's readings: shape, points of the factory)

bases.lodge: Indoors in the lodges by the river (T-3528's record, which gives no lodge to a family). Which lodge each sleeps in, and the hours, are this reading's.
bases.lodge_work: Ordinary work of a family camp at the yard the record draws (hearths, rack, mortar, woodpile, scaffold, hide frame, canoes). The tasks and hours are this reading's; no source gives them.
bases.meal: Cooking and eating at the hearth out of doors in the warm months; the hours are this reading's.
bases.river_round: Fishing the river from the bank below the lodges; ordinary work in the warm months, not recorded for any day.
bases.child: A child near the lodges, playing or helping; the hours are this reading's.
bases.winter: The cold months, November to March: more of the day indoors by the fire, the men out hunting through the middle of it. That this family winters here at all is the owner's choice (2026-11-09) and reconstructed; Wau-Bun has most families go to their wintering grounds (fact wintering).
bases.away: Off the scene for the span.
bases.trade: A trading morning at the government factory outside the fort, which Matthew Irwin kept until he left on 5 July 1812: furs and maple sugar for cloth, kettles and powder (facts traders, sugar). The canoe trip is off the scene; the day and hours are this reading's.
bases.aug15: 15 August 1812. Heald counts 'between four and five hundred' warriors in the attack, of the 500 Helm counted; which men fought no source records, and that these two were among them is reconstructed (as native_cards_1812.py grades every man of 16 to 55 of the gathering). Nothing of the fighting is drawn.
